title: Sam Parr on writing, copy and growth: how The Hustle got to 150K subscribers in year one
summary: Sam Parr explains how he built The Hustle's newsletter audience: do the email math, siphon traffic from subreddits with viral stunts, and obsess over headlines and welcome copy. He also covers hiring writers, copy work, memorable phrasing, and defining what a brand stands against.

principles.text: Go where your target audience already gathers and siphon them off; use viral stunts in niche communities.
principles.quote: my whole strategy was go to where the people who you want already are and siphon them off

principles.text: Do the math on owned channels: email reaches a subscriber daily, unlike a website people must keep returning to.
principles.quote: if I get a million people to subscribe to my newsletter and I email them every day I bet you I could make like $2 million a month doing that

principles.text: Don't ignore the 'forgotten text' like thank-you pages and welcome emails; make them good.
principles.quote: that was like the whole trick was like the Forgotten text it always has to be good

principles.text: Study a company's early copy via the web archive, not its polished current version.
principles.quote: you got to go to web archive

principles.text: Headlines matter: you can lift click-through from 1% to 10%, and long pieces just need a slippery slope.
principles.quote: you got to spend time on the headline because you can change 1% to 10% pretty easily

principles.text: Hire writers by buying stock early: find people writing for fun and probe the bottom fourth of their resume.
principles.quote: I'm going to buy her stock early before the market finds out
